note.after_visit_summary: You came in today with chest pressure that happens when you exert yourself, like walking uphill or carrying groceries, and goes away with rest. This is consistent with stable angina, which means your heart isn't getting enough blood when it works hard, likely due to narrowed arteries. Your exam and ECG were normal, which can happen even with this condition. We are concerned because of your history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and past smoking. To evaluate your heart further, you will have a nuclear stress test within the next two weeks, along with blood tests for cholesterol and kidney function. In the meantime, start taking aspirin 81 mg once daily and metoprolol 25 mg once daily. Continue your lisinopril 20 mg once daily. Increase your atorvastatin to 80 mg once nightly. Use nitroglycerin 0.4 mg under the tongue if chest pain occurs and does not go away with rest; you may repeat every 5 minutes up to three doses. If you have chest pain at rest, pain lasting more than 15 minutes, or pain not relieved by one nitroglycerin, call 911 immediately—do not drive yourself. Avoid heavy lifting and walking up the hill to your house until after your stress test. We will call you at 555-0163 to schedule the test and see you afterward to discuss results.
